data.title: Dow Jones Top Markets Headlines at 5 PM ET: The Week the Cracks in the AI Trade Grew Deeper | Cryptocurrencies ...
data.description:
The Week the Cracks in the AI Trade Grew Deeper

Intel suffered worst-ever daily decline as investors' anxieties hit new highs.

----

Cryptocurrencies Pare Losses After $6.3 Billion Hack Spooks Markets

Bitcoin and Ethereum clawed back some ground after tumbling more than 3% each on news of the major breach at the world's biggest crypto exchange.

----

U.S. Stocks Slide as Amazon, Intel Earnings Spark More AI Selling

U.S. stocks fell as the artificial-intelligence selloff began to feed on itself following more disappointing earnings reports from Amazon and Intel, leaving investors to wonder if the tech correction could become a speculative bust.

----

Fed Needs to Implement at Least Two More Rate Increases, Dallas Fed's Logan Says

Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan said at least two more 25-basis-point rate increases are needed given the current economic outlook.

----

Fed's Musalem Says Additional Firming of Monetary Policy Will Be Necessary, and Soon

St. Louis Fed President said that incremental adjustments to policy made earlier are usually less disruptive than larger, and abrupt actions taken later.

----

Oil Prices Rise as Middle East, Ukraine-Russia Conflict Fuel Supply Worries

Oil prices rose with the market on edge about possible military escalation in the Middle East, while an attack on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, Houthi claims of more attacks on Saudi refineries and a Ukrainian strike on a Russian refinery fed supply concerns.

----

Global Bond Yields Fall Sharply in October Amid Flight to Safety

Global bond yields were poised to end October sharply lower as a flight to safety revived demand for government debt, even as markets braced for higher short-term borrowing from the U.S. Treasury.

----

Canada Deems Vancouver Port Expansion a National Priority in Bid to Diversify Trade

Canada argues that the proposed expansion at the nation's busiest port is necessary for the country to meet its goal of doubling non-U.S. exports by 2035.

----

Canada GDP Seen Dipping After Two Flat Months

Canada's economy cooled in the latest quarter after activity unexpectedly stalled two months running and early data points to a slight contraction in September.

----

Eurozone Economy Slows as French Debt Worries Mount

The economy slowed in the face of high energy prices, while France's economy contracted-deepening concerns over the government's debt load amid political paralysis.

----

Bank of Japan Declares Inflation Win, Clearing Way for Rate Hikes

Friday's hold was widely expected, giving more time for previous hikes, including one in September, to feed through to the economy.

----

BOE Survey Points to Faster Price Rises, But Slowing Wage Growth

Businesses expected the prices they charge to rise by 3.8% over the coming 12 months, an increase from the 3.7% expected in September.

----

Ukraine Hits Russian Oil Refinery, Ending Pause and Defying Trump

The first strike on a Russian oil refinery in two weeks comes after Russian attacks killed 27 civilians on Thursday.

----

Week Ahead for FX, Bonds: U.S. Midterms, Jobs Data in Focus

Outside the U.S., interest-rate decisions are due from the Bank of England, Sweden's Riksbank, Australia's RBA and central banks in Norway, Czech Republic, Malaysia, Brazil and Mexico. 




  (END) Dow Jones Newswires

data.title: Fujifilm to Increase Production Capacity by 5x for Magnetic Data Storage Tape
data.description:
Fujifilm to Increase Production Capacity by 5x for Magnetic Data Storage Tape

Investing approximately 10 billion yen to meet growing data archiving demand driven by the spread of generative AI, strengthening stable supply of the latest-generation “FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10”

FUJIFILM Corporation will invest approximately 10 billion yen at its Kanagawa Factory, Odawara Site, to increase its production capacity for data storage magnetic tape by approximately five times*1. The investment will strengthen Fujifilm’s stable supply system for magnetic tape in response to growing data archiving demand accompanying the spread of generative AI. This investment, to be made from fiscal 2026 through fiscal 2028, will be used to expand manufacturing facilities and increase personnel to strengthen the production structure.

The rapid spread of generative AI and cloud services is driving exponential growth in the volume of data generated worldwide. As a result, establishing environments in which the enormous amounts of data accumulated through AI training and inference as well as the digitalization of business activities can be stored and utilized securely and efficiently is becoming increasingly important in supporting the digital society. Magnetic tape can store large volumes of data over long periods at low cost and can also be physically isolated from networks.

In recent years, the use of magnetic tape has been expanding, particularly among major cloud service providers and data center operators. Furthermore, given the sophistication of cyberattacks, magnetic tape is attracting increasing attention as a means of protecting data from threats such as ransomware.

Fujifilm began research into magnetic tape in the 1950s and subsequently expanded its business in response to changing data recording and storage needs, including the launch of broadcast videotape and consumer high-definition videotape. Since launching “FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium1” data storage magnetic tape in 2000, Fujifilm has worked to improve magnetic tape performance by leveraging its proprietary materials technologies and precision coating technologies. In 2011, Fujifilm became the first company in the world to commercialize Barium Ferrite (BaFe) magnetic particles*2 for use in magnetic tape. In 2025, the company launched the latest-generation “FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10,” which uses proprietary “fine hybrid magnetic particles”*3 combining technologies for BaFe and Strontium Ferrite (SrFe) magnetic particles*4. Through such technological innovation, Fujifilm has led advances in magnetic tape capacity and currently holds the top global share of the magnetic tape market*5.

Through this investment, Fujifilm will expand manufacturing facilities, primarily for its latest-generation “FUJIFILM LTO Ultrium10” data storage magnetic tape, and increase personnel to ensure stable supply. The approximately 10 billion yen investment represents the largest investment Fujifilm has made to date in dedicated facilities for LTO tape. Fujifilm will enhance its ability to meet the growing demand for data archiving while ensuring a more stable supply to customers.

Fujifilm will continue to support the long-term storage of growing volumes of data accompanying the spread of generative AI and cloud services through higher-capacity magnetic tape and stable supply, thereby contributing to the realization of a sustainable digital society.

About Fujifilm

FUJIFILM North America Corporation, a marketing subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings America Corporation, consists of five operating divisions. The Imaging Division provides consumer and commercial photographic products and services, including silver halide consumables; inkjet consumables; digital printing equipment, along with service and support; personalized photo products fulfillment; film; one-time-use cameras; and the popular instax™ line of instant cameras, smartphone printers, instant film, and accessories. The Electronic Imaging Division markets its GFX System and X Series lines of mirrorless digital cameras, lenses, and accessories to provide a variety of content creation solutions for both still and moving imagery. The Optical Devices Division provides optical lenses for the broadcast, cinematography, closed circuit television, videography, and industrial markets, and also markets binoculars and other optical imaging solutions. The Business Innovation Division offers a full lineup of digital print and toner technologies focused on enabling the digital transformation of businesses and print shops with its offerings of multifunction printers, digital inkjet presses, production toner printers, software, and more. The Industrial Products Division delivers new products derived from Fujifilm technologies including data storage tape products, including OEM and FUJIFILM Ultrium LTO cartridges, desalination solutions, microfilters and gas separation membranes.

For more information, please visit https://www.fujifilm.com/us/en/about/region, go to https://x.com/fujifilmus to follow Fujifilm on X, or go to https://www.facebook.com/FujifilmAmerica to Like Fujifilm on Facebook.

FUJIFILM Corporation is a subsidiary of FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation. FUJIFILM Holdings Corporation, headquartered in Tokyo, leverages its depth of knowledge and proprietary core technologies to deliver innovative products and services across the globe through the four key business segments of healthcare, electronics, business innovation, and imaging with over 70,000 employees. Guided and united by our Group Purpose of “giving our world more smiles,” we address social challenges and create a positive impact on society through our products, services, and business operations. Under its medium-term management plan, VISION2030, which ends in FY2030, we aspire to continue our evolution into a company that creates value and smiles for various stakeholders as a collection of global leading businesses and achieve a global revenue of 4 trillion yen (29 billion USD at an exchange rate of 140 JPY/USD). For more information, please visit: www.fujifilmholdings.com.

For further details about our commitment to sustainability and Fujifilm’s Sustainable Value Plan 2030, click here.

  *1 Based on shipment capacity, compared with fiscal year 2025.
  *2 A proprietary magnetic material that Fujifilm was the first in the world to commercialize as a material for magnetic tape. By enabling high-density recording, it has served as a core technology supporting higher-capacity data storage magnetic tape and market expansion.
  *3 A proprietary magnetic material developed by Fujifilm by combining nanoparticle design technologies used for Barium Ferrite and Strontium Ferrite magnetic particles. Further reduction in particle size and enhanced magnetic properties enable high-density recording.
  *4 A proprietary magnetic material developed by Fujifilm to enable further increases in the capacity of data storage magnetic tape. It has extremely high magnetic properties and can maintain stable, high performance even when made into finer particles.
  *5 Producer share, according to Fujifilm.

data.title: Annovis Bio, Inc. Receives Continued Listing Standard Notice from the NYSE
data.description:
MALVERN, Pa., Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Annovis Bio, Inc. (NYSE: ANVS) (“Annovis” or the “Company”), a Phase 3 clinical-stage biotechnology company developing the investigational oral therapy, buntanetap, for neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's disease (AD) and Parkinson's disease (PD), today announced that on October 29, 2026, it received notice (the “Notice”) from the New York Stock Exchange (NYSE) that it is no longer in compliance with the NYSE continued listing standards set forth in Section 802.01B of the NYSE’s Listed Company Manual due to the fact that the Company’s average market capitalization over a consecutive 30 trading-day period was less than $50 million while its stockholders’ equity was less than $50 million.

The Notice does not affect the Company’s business operations or its reporting obligations with the Securities and Exchange Commission, and it does not conflict with or cause an event of default under any of the Company’s material debt or other agreements.

As set forth in the Notice, as of October 28, 2026, the 30 trading-day average market capitalization of the Company was approximately $48.4 million and the Company’s last reported stockholders’ deficit as of June 30, 2026 was approximately $(4.3) million.

The Company has notified the NYSE that it will submit a plan within 45 days of the Notice advising the NYSE of definitive action it has taken, or is taking, to bring it into conformity with Section 802.01B within 9 months of receipt of the Notice. The NYSE will review the Company’s plan and, within 45 days, make a determination as to whether the Company has made a reasonable demonstration of its ability to come into conformity with Section 802.01B within 9 months. If the Company’s plan is not submitted on a timely basis or is not accepted, the NYSE will initiate delisting proceedings. If the NYSE accepts the Company’s plan, the Company’s common stock will continue to be listed and traded on the NYSE during the cure period, subject to the Company’s compliance with the plan and other continued listing standards. The NYSE will review the Company on a semi-annual basis to confirm compliance with the plan. If the Company fails to comply with the plan or does not meet continued listing standards at the end of the 9-month cure period, it will be subject to the prompt initiation of NYSE suspension and delisting procedures. The NYSE may take accelerated delisting action in the event the Company’s common stock trades at levels viewed to be abnormally low. The NYSE generally views trading below a price of $0.10 to be abnormally low.

The Notice has no immediate impact on the listing of the Company’s common stock, which will continue to be “ANVS”, subject to the Company’s continued compliance with the plan and other listing requirements of the NYSE. However, the common stock trading symbol will have an added designation of “.BC” to indicate that the status of the common stock is below criteria with the NYSE continued listing standards. The “.BC” indicator will be removed at such time as the Company regains compliance.

data.title: Why Intel's stock saw its worst day in decades - and a $140 billion wipeout
data.description:
By Britney Nguyen and Nora Redmond

Intel's PC business is under pressure as memory-chip prices dent demand and as corporate IT teams have less budget for laptops

Intel shed $140 billion in market cap Friday.

Intel lost $140 billion in market capitalization on Friday as a personal-computer slowdown spooked investors.

The chip company blamed a weak PC market for a revenue forecast that came in well shy of what analysts were expecting Thursday. Intel's (INTC) outlook for the December quarter calls for revenue of between $15 billion and $16 billion, below the $17.1 billion FactSet consensus view.

PC revenue also surprisingly declined in the September quarter, helping send shares down 29% Friday following Intel's third-quarter earnings release. That marked its largest one-day drop since at least March 1980, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

The technology giant also shed $140 billion in market capitalization - its biggest one-day loss on record, the data showed.

Shares of Advanced Micro Devices (AMD), another maker of PC chips, fell 11% on Friday.

Demand has slowed for PCs as memory-chip prices have risen dramatically. Companies are also facing more limited information-technology budgets, a further factor weighing on PC demand, Intel Chief Financial Officer David Zinsner said on the company's earnings call.

For analysts at Jefferies led by Blayne Curtis, it's a positive that the revenue reset was driven by softer demand for PCs rather than a change in the trajectory of the company's data-center and AI group. However, they noted that Intel will likely continue to lose market share throughout next year, "making it tough to underwrite the longer-term story even with Foundry/packaging customer announcements."

The pressure on the PC market isn't exactly a shock given that surging memory prices have been a nagging issue all year, and one that was broadly expected to slow demand for laptops. But the negative impact "came a little sooner and deeper than we thought," John Pitzer, Intel's corporate vice president of investor relations, told MarketWatch.

Intel's outlook was also weighed down by an explosion earlier this month at one of its chip-making facilities in Israel, which Pitzer said led to a reduction of $300 million within the company's fourth-quarter forecast.

David Wagner, a portfolio manager at Aptus Capital Advisors, said in emailed comments that Intel's earnings report showed that even as it's "losing on one front" with PC chips, it's also having trouble capitalizing on strong demand for server chips given some component shortages.

Although Intel is making progress in its chip-manufacturing business, which has been a key area of interest for investors, Thursday's report showcased "the challenges the company faces in pushing its recent turnaround into a sustained recovery," eMarketer senior analyst Asa Hiken said in comments shared with MarketWatch.

Demand for Intel's central processing units for data-center servers has surged this year as agentic artificial intelligence has taken off. That has been a boon for the company, which less than a year ago faced questions over its place in an AI world that at the time was mostly focused on graphics processing units like those made by Nvidia (NVDA).

But server CPU demand isn't enough on its own to support Intel through near-term challenges, Hiken said, namely the ongoing weakness in the PC market.

The sustainability of Intel's growth will come down largely to its foundry business, Hiken said. Intel's advanced chip-packaging technology is gaining attention from customers and is viewed by Wall Street as one of the more promising aspects of its chip-manufacturing business.

However, the costs for building chips are massive, Hiken noted, and Intel still needs to secure meaningful commitments from customers who want to use its foundry. Until then, investors will continue to question the viability of this business and the steep investments being poured into it, he added.

For a team at Morgan Stanley led by Joseph Moore, Intel's stock isn't compelling even after its selloff. They see the company losing market share to its fabless competitors that have lower capital-spending requirements, with expectations for Advanced Micro Devices, Nvidia, Graviton and Axion to all materially outgrow Intel's 30% market growth rate in CPUs in 2027.

-Britney Nguyen -Nora Redmond

data.title: Goranson Bain Ausley Ranks No. 6 Among Dallas Business Journal's Best Places to Work for 2026
data.description:
Goranson Bain Ausley Ranks No. 6 Among Dallas Business Journal's Best Places to Work for 2026

Goranson Bain Ausley Ranks No. 6 Among Dallas Business Journal's Best Places to Work for 2026

PR Newswire

DALLAS, Oct. 30, 2026

Employee survey highlights the firm's supportive culture, commitment to professional development, and high employee engagement.

DALLAS, Oct. 30, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- Goranson Bain Ausley (GBA), Texas's largest law firm devoted exclusively to family law, ranked No. 6 in the medium-sized category of the Dallas Business Journal's 2026 Best Places to Work. The recognition reflects the firm's longstanding commitment to creating a workplace where attorneys and staff feel valued, supported, and equipped to provide exceptional service to clients.

The award is based on confidential employee feedback measuring workplace culture, leadership, engagement, and satisfaction. GBA earned an overall score of 94.79 out of 100, with 96.43% of participating employees classified as highly engaged and no employees classified as disengaged. When asked to describe their workplace in one word, employees most frequently chose "supportive."

One employee connected the firm's culture directly to its purpose:

"Our firm's mission is to help people see possibilities they couldn't see before. Of course this applies to our divorce clients, who find themselves at one of the most difficult crossroads in their lives, and often come to us in despair about what the future might hold. It equally applies to our team."

"Our people are the reason GBA has been able to grow while maintaining the culture that makes this firm special," said Lindley Bain, Managing Partner of Goranson Bain Ausley. "We want every member of our team to feel respected, supported, and confident that their contributions matter. That commitment extends to our clients, who benefit from a team that genuinely cares about each other and the people we serve."

Employee responses highlighted the firm's emphasis on professional development, collaboration, work-life balance, and leadership that values people. GBA supports attorneys and staff through continuing education, Board Certification, Collaborative Law training, mentoring, and opportunities for professional advancement.

As GBA has grown to more than 55 attorneys across eight Texas offices, maintaining a strong, connected workplace has remained a priority. The firm's approach combines the resources and experience of a statewide practice with collegial local teams and a shared commitment to client service.

The Dallas Business Journal's Best Places to Work program recognizes North Texas organizations based on employee feedback and measures factors associated with employee engagement and workplace satisfaction. The medium-sized company category includes organizations with 50 to 249 local employees.

About Goranson Bain Ausley

Founded in 1987, Goranson Bain Ausley is Texas's largest law firm focused exclusively on family law. Its more than 55 attorneys serve clients from eight offices in Dallas, Plano, Fort Worth, Granbury, Austin, San Antonio, Midland, and Flower Mound. More than 30 of its attorneys are Board Certified in Family Law by the Texas Board of Legal Specialization. The firm's people are its greatest asset: accomplished attorneys recognized for their expertise, integrity, sound judgment, and dedication to clients. The firm's practice encompasses complex divorce, high-net-worth property division, child custody, mediation, Collaborative Divorce, and appeals.

Learn more at www.gbfamilylaw.com.

data.title: United States Lime & Minerals Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results and Declares Regular Quarterly Cash Dividend
data.description:
DALLAS, Oct. 30, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- United States Lime & Minerals, Inc. (NASDAQ: USLM) today reported third quarter 2026 results: The Company’s revenues in the third quarter 2026 were $106.2 million, compared to $102.0 million in the third quarter 2025, an increase of $4.2 million, or 4.1%. For the first nine months 2026, the Company’s revenues were $293.1 million, compared to $284.8 million in the first nine months 2025, an increase of $8.4 million, or 2.9%. The increase in revenues in the third quarter 2026, compared to the third quarter 2025, resulted primarily from modest increases in both average sales prices and sales volumes. Increased sales volumes were principally due to increased demand from the Company’s steel customers, partially offset by reduced demand from the Company’s construction customers. The increase in revenues in the first nine months 2026, compared to the first nine months 2025, resulted primarily from modest increases in both average sales prices and sales volumes. Increased sales volumes were principally due to increased demand from the Company’s steel customers, partially offset by reduced demand from the Company’s roof shingle customers.

The Company’s gross profit was $50.8 million in the third quarter 2026, compared to $52.2 million in the third quarter 2025, a decrease of $1.4 million, or 2.7%. The Company’s gross profit was $139.2 million in the first nine months 2026, compared to $140.2 million in the first nine months 2025, a decrease of $1.0 million, or 0.7%. The decreases in gross profit in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to the comparable 2025 periods, resulted primarily from higher transportation and fuel costs, driven principally by higher diesel costs, and production inefficiencies experienced during the integration of our new Texas kiln into our existing plant operations.

Selling, general and administrative (“SG&A”) expenses were $6.1 million in the third quarter 2026, compared to $5.9 million in the third quarter 2025, an increase of $0.1 million, or 2.3%. SG&A expenses were $18.1 million in the first nine months 2026, compared to $18.4 million in the first nine months 2025, a decrease of $0.3 million, or 1.5%.

Other (income) expense, net was $3.8 million and $10.4 million income in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to $3.4 million and $9.6 million income in the third quarter and first nine months 2025, increases of $0.4 million and $0.8 million, respectively. The increases in other (income) expense, net for the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to the comparable 2025 periods, were primarily due to interest earned on higher average balances of cash and cash equivalents.

The Company reported net income of $38.0 million ($1.32 per share diluted) and $103.1 million ($3.58 per share diluted) in the third quarter and first nine months 2026, compared to $38.8 million ($1.35 per share diluted) and $103.7 million ($3.61 per share diluted) in the third quarter and first nine months 2025, decreases of $0.7 million, or 1.9%, and $0.6 million, or 0.6%, respectively.

“We saw modest increases in both volumes and sales prices for our lime and limestone products in the third quarter 2026, while our expenses reflected the impact of the sharp rise in diesel prices,” said Timothy W. Byrne, President and Chief Executive Officer. “Although we remain optimistic regarding overall construction demand in the future, certain large construction projects have recently experienced delays for various reasons, including securing permits, and we are monitoring indications that Texas’ residential construction is beginning to slow down. The new kiln at our Texas facility began intermittently producing quicklime in the third quarter, and we expect to have final commissioning completed in the fourth quarter. To that end, our costs in Texas have been impacted by production inefficiencies as we continue to integrate the new kiln into our existing plant operations,” Mr. Byrne added.

Dividend

The Company announced today that the Board of Directors has declared a regular quarterly cash dividend of $0.06 per share on the Company’s common stock. This dividend is payable on December 11, 2026 to stockholders of record at the close of business on November 20, 2026.

United States Lime & Minerals, Inc., a NASDAQ-listed public company with headquarters in Dallas, Texas, is a manufacturer of lime and limestone products, supplying primarily the construction (including highway, road, and building contractors), industrial (including paper and glass manufacturers), environmental (including municipal sanitation and water treatment facilities and flue gas treatment processes), metals (including steel producers), roof shingle manufacturers, agriculture (including poultry producers), and oil and gas services industries. The Company operates lime and limestone plants and distribution facilities in Arkansas, Colorado, Louisiana, Missouri, Oklahoma, and Texas through its wholly owned subsidiaries, Arkansas Lime Company, ART Quarry TRS LLC (DBA Carthage Crushed Limestone), Colorado Lime Company, Mill Creek Dolomite, LLC, Texas Lime Company, U.S. Lime Company, U.S. Lime Company-Shreveport, U.S. Lime Company-St. Clair, and U.S. Lime Company-Transportation. In addition, the Company, through its wholly owned subsidiary, U.S. Lime Company-O & G, LLC, has royalty and non-operated working interests in natural gas wells located in Johnson County, Texas, in the Barnett Shale Formation.

Any statements contained in this News Release, including, but not limited to, statements relating to demand, costs, production, and the new Texas kiln, that are not statements of historical fact are forward-looking statements as defined in the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. The Company undertakes no obligation to publicly update or revise any forward-looking statements, and investors are cautioned that such statements involve risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from expectations, including without limitation those risks and uncertainties indicated from time to time in the Company’s filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission.

data.title: AM Best Upgrades Credit Ratings of Patria Re (US), Inc.
data.description:
AM Best Upgrades Credit Ratings of Patria Re (US), Inc.

AM Best has upgraded the Financial Strength Rating to A- (Excellent) from B++ (Good) and the Long-Term Issuer Credit Rating to “a- “(Excellent) from “bbb+” (Good) of Patria Re (US), Inc. (Patria US) (Charleston, SC). The outlook of these Credit Ratings (ratings) is stable.

The ratings reflect Patria US’ balance sheet strength, which AM Best assesses as very strong, as well as its adequate operating performance, limited business profile and appropriate enterprise risk management (ERM).

The rating upgrades reflect Patria US’ improved risk-adjusted capitalization, as measured by Best’s Capital Adequacy Ratio (BCAR), derived from a substantial capital injection by Grupo Peña Verde, and supported by strong positive bottom-line results.

The stable outlooks reflect the support Patria US receives from its group, which translates into capital contributions when required, as well as profitable business cessions to back up growth, given the strategic importance of the entity.

The ratings also recognize Patria US’ affiliation and strategic importance to its ultimate parent, Peña Verde, S.A.B. (Peña Verde), a leading group in Mexico’s insurance and reinsurance industries, which provides synergies and operating efficiencies. The ratings also reflect the support received from its sister company, Reaseguradora Patria, S.A. (Patria Re), the lead company of the Peña Verde group and a well-known reinsurer in Latin America. As of June 2026, Peña Verde had equity of USD 937 million and premiums of USD 709 million. Patria US is considered a new company formation as it began operations in February of 2023 after receiving authorization in the United States from the South Carolina Department of Insurance. The company was created and is domiciled in South Carolina, as part of Peña Verde’s efforts to expand and strengthen its operations.

AM Best considers Patria US’ balance sheet strength to be at the very strong level, with its capital base expected to strengthen from positive bottom-line results. The company has received three capital contributions; the most recent capital infusion took place in August 2026, which amounted to USD 50 million. AM Best will monitor the company’s capital inflows to continue assessing its capability to grow and undertake its desired level of risk.

Patria US’ operating performance is considered adequate. The company’s initial bulk of business consists of a diverse mix of premiums retroceded by Patria Re, with a profitable track record. Synergies with Patria Re are expected to help keep operating expenses stable, as Patria US’ operation continues to grow. The company reported a USD 3.92 million profit during 2025, and as of June 2026, Patria US has reported positive bottom-line results of USD 1.7 million, achieved through premium sufficiency. AM Best will continue to monitor the underwriting quality and operating expenses to further assess this building block assessment.

Peña Verde and Patria Re have established a solid niche position in Mexico and in other Latin America markets; however, Patria US’ business profile is considered limited, given its current strategic role within the group.

Patria US shares all the group’s comprehensive ERM infrastructure and practices, as well as the expertise from its shared management team. AM Best considers the company’s ERM assessment as appropriate for its risk appetite and as being strongly supported by the holding company’s back office.

Positive rating actions could occur if Patria Re (US), Inc., is able to successfully execute its business plan on increasing its U.S. operations and expanding premium sources, while maintaining consistent and profitable results in the long term.

Negative rating actions could also take place if a sustained deterioration of risk-adjusted capitalization occurs driven by unfavorable results, or the support and plans the group has for Patria US negatively change in AM Best’s opinion.

This press release relates to Credit Ratings that have been published on AM Best’s website. For all rating information relating to the release and pertinent disclosures, including details of the office responsible for issuing each of the individual ratings referenced in this release, please see AM Best’s Recent Rating Activity web page. For additional information regarding the use and limitations of Credit Rating opinions, please view Guide to Best’s Credit Ratings. For information on the proper use of Best’s Credit Ratings, Best’s Performance Assessments, Best’s Preliminary Credit Assessments and AM Best press releases, please view Guide to Proper Use of Best’s Ratings & Assessments.

AM Best is a global credit rating agency, news publisher and data analytics provider specializing in the insurance industry. Headquartered in the United States, the company does business in over 100 countries with regional offices in London, Amsterdam, Dubai, Hong Kong, Singapore and Mexico City.
